title: Merging and concatenating
summary: Joining tables on a key with merge (inner, left, indicator), finding rows with no match, and stacking frames with concat.
hints: `orders_with_customers`: `orders.merge(customers, on="customer_id", how="inner")` adds the customer columns to each order; then `.sort_values("order_id").reset_index(drop=True)`. Orders whose customer is unknown disappear in an inner join.

`customers_without_orders`: `customers[~customers["customer_id"].isin(orders["customer_id"])]["name"].tolist()`. `unknown_customer_orders`: merge `orders` *left* onto `customers[["customer_id"]]` with `indicator=True`; rows whose `_merge` is `"left_only"` had no match.

`revenue_by_city`: start from the customers so every city appears: `customers.merge(orders, on="customer_id", how="left")`, then `groupby("city")["amount"].sum()`; `sum` treats the NaN amounts of customers without orders as 0. `stack_months`: `pd.concat([jan.assign(month="jan"), feb.assign(month="feb")], ignore_index=True)`.
